reason: The cited code exists verbatim and is reachable, but the security claim does not hold. The literal 5 is not an arbitrary magic-number cap on attacker-controlled content: it is the exact number of pickle streams in PyTorch's legacy (non-zip) serialization format. torch's _legacy_save writes exactly five pickles (MAGIC_NUMBER, PROTOCOL_VERSION, sys_info, the object, serialized_storage_keys) and _legacy_load performs exactly five pickle loads before switching to raw storage reads (_set_from_file). picklescan deliberately mirrors that loader (src/picklescan/torch.py:17-19 and 50-73 are verbatim copies of torch/serialization.py with upstream permalinks; scanner.py:522-524 reproduces _legacy_load's magic-number precheck), and get_magic_number seeks back to offset 0 (torch.py:80) so iterations 1-5 cover streams 1-5 with no off-by-one leaving the object pickle unscanned. Therefore a 6th or later concatenated pickle stream is never deserialized by torch.load -- it lands in the region torch reads as raw tensor storage bytes, or is never read at all -- so it cannot execute a REDUCE/GLOBAL payload. There is no scanner/loader parity gap and thus no detection bypass (CWE-184 does not apply); scanning past stream 5 would instead disassemble raw tensor data and produce false positives, which is why multiple_pickles=False is used.
